prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s “Contract with You” presents a 100‑day, common‑sense plan to fix a broken system the party says has been failed by both Conservatives and Labour. It promises to take back control of borders, money and laws; restore British culture, identity and values; cut waste and taxes; end “woke” capture in institutions; and unlock homegrown energy to deliver growth, lower bills and secure sovereignty.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop the small boats by leaving the ECHR, detaining and deporting illegal entrants, and returning boats to France.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at the point of use, using all available capacity and cutting waste; tax breaks to retain and recruit staff.
- Make work pay: raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Scrap Net Zero and green levies to cut household bills by £500; fast‑track North Sea oil and gas and test shale.
- Slash government waste and bureaucracy; redirect money to frontline services.

Borders and immigration
- New Department of Immigration; bar asylum from safe countries; no legal aid for non‑citizens; immediate deportation of foreign criminals.
- Bar student dependents; 5‑year residency and work requirement for benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax (NI at 20% for foreign hires, exempt essential health/care and micro‑firms) to fund UK training.

Economy and tax
- Personal: cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies; big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; abolish IHT below £2m (20% above, with charity option).
- Business: lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; axe business rates for high‑street SMEs (offset by 4% online delivery tax); simplify planning; scrap EU‑style red tape and ease hiring/firing; radically simplify the tax code.

NHS
- Zero waiting lists via independent/not‑for‑profit capacity; 0% basic rate tax for NHS and care staff for 3 years; end training caps and write off fees over service; patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation wait limits are missed; weekend theatres; clamp down on waste; Pharmacy‑First drive; inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.

Energy and Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; license North Sea oil/gas; 2‑year shale test; accelerate SMRs and other clean tech.

Law, order and justice
- 40,000 frontline officers, zero‑tolerance policing, more stop and search; end “woke” policies; automatic life for violent repeat offenders; expand courts; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new detention places.

Education and culture
- Patriotic curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap interest on student loans, tighten standards; protect free speech in universities; more PRUs and firm exclusions.

Welfare
- Toughen work requirements (2‑strike rule); face‑to‑face assessments; focus on youth back‑to‑work.

Brexit and sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the TCA.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% within 6 years; pay rises; legal protections for forces; full veterans department; procurement reform.

Housing and families
- Fast‑track brownfield building; prioritize locals for social housing; scrap Section 24; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.
- Marriage tax allowance (25% transferable) when affordable; front‑load child benefit; mandate single‑sex spaces; curb social‑media harms.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap HS2; end the war on drivers (ban ULEZ/LTNs, roll back blanket 20mph); new 50/50 UK‑owned utility model; single infrastructure fund.

Agriculture and fishing
- Boost farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate‑linked farm subsidies; protect country sports.
- Reclaim fisheries: license/charge foreign boats, ban supertrawlers; rebuild UK fleet and processing.

Constitution and “Reclaiming Britain”
- Leave ECHR; reform Lords and Civil Service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Reject WEF/WHO overreach and CBDC; replace the Equalities Act; comprehensive Free Speech Bill; reform/scrap BBC licence; national days; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding
- Claimed savings: £150bn pa + £10bn pa from growth; costs: £141bn pa.
